q.t: Stars shine with…
q.e: Stars make their own light.

q.t: The star closest to us is…
q.e: The Sun is a star — the closest one.

q.t: The brightest star in the night sky is…
q.e: Sirius, in Canis Major.

q.t: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
q.e: Its soil is reddish.

q.t: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
q.e: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

q.t: How many natural satellites does Earth have?
q.e: One — the Moon. Mars has 2.

q.t: The Moon takes about how many days to revolve around the Earth?
q.e: About 27 days.

q.t: Constellation Orion is imagined as a…
q.e: Three stars in the middle form his belt.

q.t: The Pole Star is called…
q.e: It appears nearly stationary in the north.

q.t: Excessive artificial light at night is…
q.e: It hides most stars in cities.

q.t: How many constellations does the IAU list?
q.e: The entire sky is divided into 88 regions.

q.t: Why did ancient people recognise star patterns?
q.e: Sailors and travellers used stars to find direction.

q.t: Venus is called the Morning or Evening Star, but it is…
q.e: It shines brightly at dawn and dusk.

q.t: How can you tell a planet from a star with the naked eye?
o: Stars twinkle a lot; planets don't
q.e: That's the easiest test.

q.t: The inner four planets are…
q.e: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars.

q.t: The outer four planets are…
o: Large, mostly gas and ice, with rings
q.e: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

q.t: The asteroid belt lies between…
q.e: Many rocky asteroids orbit there.

q.t: A comet's tail forms because…
o: Its frozen material evaporates near the Sun
q.e: Moving away from the Sun, it grows dim.

q.t: Sirius is in the constellation…
q.e: Orion's dog.

q.t: The Pole Star belongs to…
q.e: The Big Dipper (Saptaṛiṣhi) is in Ursa Major.

q.t: Why does the Sun look huge but other stars look like dots?
o: The Sun is the biggest star
q.e: Some stars are bigger than the Sun but far away.

q.t: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury though farther from the Sun?
q.e: An atmosphere can trap heat.

q.t: How do you find the Pole Star from the Big Dipper?
o: Extend the line through the two end stars of its cup about 5 times their gap
q.e: That leads to a not-very-bright star — Polaris.

q.t: Why do Moon craters last so long?
o: No atmosphere, water or life to erode them
q.e: On Earth, wind and water would wear them down.

q.t: Why can't the Pole Star be seen from the Southern Hemisphere?
q.e: It's useful for north only in the Northern Hemisphere.

q.t: 1 astronomical unit (au) is about…
q.e: About 150 million km.

q.t: Why was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
o: More similar small objects were found and 'planet' was redefined
q.e: The IAU redefined the word.

q.t: Chandrayaan-3 made India the first country to land near the Moon's…
q.e: Vikram lander with Pragyan rover, 23 August 2023.

q.t: 23 August is celebrated as…
q.e: Marking Chandrayaan-3's landing.

q.t: Why wait about half an hour in the dark before stargazing?
q.e: Adjusted eyes see far more stars.

q.t: The Sun's diameter is about how many times the Earth's?
q.e: About 100 times bigger in diameter.

q.t: The Moon's diameter is about what fraction of the Earth's?
q.e: About ¼ the size.

q.t: The Moon is about how far from Earth?
q.e: Our nearest neighbour in space.

q.t: Proxima Centauri is about 269,000 au away. This means it is…
o: 269,000 times as far as the Sun
q.e: It's the nearest star after the Sun.

q.t: Planets get most energy from the Sun, so generally…
q.e: Except where an atmosphere traps heat, like Venus.

q.t: Why is Earth called the Blue Planet?
o: Much of its surface is covered with water
q.e: From space it appears blue.

q.t: Orion is best seen from India during…
q.e: After sunset in those months.

q.t: To find Sirius from Orion, extend the belt line towards the…
q.e: The belt's three stars point to Sirius.

q.t: Today a constellation means…
o: A defined region of the sky
q.e: Originally a pattern, now one of 88 regions.

q.t: Chandrayaan-4 aims to…
o: Bring back lunar soil and rock samples
q.e: A sample-return mission.
